source.purpose: Confirm urlsplit parsing is not input validation and reconstructed URLs may normalize URL spelling, relevant to staged source identity read-back.
source.cost_quota: free public Python documentation; no API key or credits
source.reliability_limits: Documentation describes Python parser behavior; repo-specific canonical policy and its CI enforcement are separate and must be tested.

learning.title: Staged URL identities must be canonical before research read-back
learning.claim: Python urllib.parse.urlsplit() parses URL components but does not validate all inputs; URL recombination can normalize scheme casing or remove empty components, so staged identity evidence must require the raw stored URL to equal the canonicalized URL before reporting a source as verified.
learning.decision: STAGED_CANONICAL_URL_READBACK_GATE: Reject a staged source when canonicalize(raw_url) != raw_url even if its source_id matches the normalized URL. Verify unique source and learning identities and references, then read back the staged file. Use positive canonical and negative uppercase-scheme regression tests; never count an unverified candidate as new or overwrite canonical history.
learning.next_measurement: On PR #326 latest HEAD run python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_*.py and verify 4 PR workflows, then reconcile against current main and read back any approved merge. Confirm reporter rejects noncanonical staged source while retaining 90/75 historical rows.
failure_history: 2026-10-26 PR #326 staged identity validation accepted noncanonical raw source URL if normalized source_id matched; canonical ledger validation was stricter.
